title: the plugin's value is measured, not asserted
description: Tasks: (1) Pilot: one paid /audit:run end to end on the benchmark fixture, hard cap 4.50 USD (--max-budget-usd), recording what the orchestrator prose drives, cost per stage and where it stalls; this unblocks the decision on moving prose rules into scripts. (2) Design a subscription-based comparison: one feature-sized task in a brownfield fixture repo with hidden acceptance tests; arms = plain Claude Code, Claude Code with the same skills and a short CLAUDE.md, and the plugin's pipeline; same model, pinned CLI version, same skills, fresh session per run, randomized order; measure acceptance tests, out-of-scope changes, false completion claims, human interventions, wall clock, tokens and list-price equivalent, and share of the subscription window; scenarios: feature, bugfix, interrupted session plus resume, a step a guard must stop. (3) Run it within an agreed subscription time budget, n>=2 per arm, and publish the result with its limits.
desiredOutcome: one end-to-end pipeline run on a fixture shows what a task costs and delivers through the plugin's own commands, and a reproducible with/without comparison on a feature-sized task reports outcome, cost, time and interventions per arm

tasks.title: one paid /audit:run on the bench fixture shows cost per stage and where the pipeline stalls
tasks.description: The orchestrator runs this, not an executor. The user allotted 5 USD for it on 2026-10-06, so no second paid run is made without asking again. It is one paid `claude -p "/audit:run P1.1"` on the bench fixture, with `--max-budget-usd 4.50` as the hard cap, run through the quality-gates-internal harness at reports/2026-10-05-deep-analysis/fixtures/bench/: build_bench_repo.sh's plugin arm with bench-manifest.json, export_plugin.sh re-pinned from b090fbd5 to the commit under test, run_bench.sh with prompt.txt replaced by the command and keeping the model and effort it already pins, and extract_metrics.py and quality_check.py unchanged. The adapted arm file allows exactly the plugin's own script calls and the git verbs the pipeline needs, and the report lists every allow rule that had to be added, because the probe's arm file allowed only the test command and read-only git. The report records what the orchestrator prose drove (which reference files were read, and their bytes), tokens and list-price cost per stage (main loop, executor, reviewer, gate, close), turns and wall clock per stage, permission denials, where the run stalled or stopped, and the quality_check verdict. Every figure sits beside the command that re-derives it from the run's stream, the document names no machine path, and its findings are the input P106 waits on before moving prose rules into scripts.

outcome.technical: One paid `claude -p "/audit:run P1.1"` was made by the orchestrator on 2026-10-06 against local main b6d9a4a31d2a, through an adapted copy of the bench harness (plugin arm, export re-pinned to the commit under test, the probe's model and effort kept, --max-budget-usd 4.50, --max-turns 30, acceptEdits with --permission-prompts none, an isolated settings file with no blanket Bash rule; extract_metrics.py and quality_check.py byte-identical to the originals). Result: success in 19 turns and 131.9 s, total_cost_usd 1.2878 (list-price equivalent), no permission denial, quality_check PASS on every criterion. docs/research/pipeline-pilot.md reports what the orchestrator prose drove (the reference files and their bytes), tokens and apportioned cost, requests and wall clock per stage from a split script kept with the artifacts - the main loop before any dispatch carries the largest share (0.7735 of 1.2878 USD, 49.6 s), the executor and reviewer together about 0.13 USD - every allow rule the arm added (only two were ever used, because the main loop's script calls were pre-approved by run.md's allowed-tools, an inference the report labels as such), and how each predicted stall point turned out: the stamp went stale only because the orchestrator's first --record created the evidence ledger between the executor's take and the compare (observed); a > in the done note did not trip anything; and further findings for the scripts-over-prose phase - the main loop moved the phase to in_progress by editing the manifest by hand, guessed argv twice, the executor read a test exit code through a pipe, the TDD reminder told a regression-mode executor to add tests, and the plugin's usage line disagrees with the session's total. Every figure sits beside the command that re-derives it; no machine path is named; the artifacts are kept in the internal analysis folder.
outcome.descriptive: One real, capped run of the plugin's pipeline on a small bug fixed it correctly for about a dollar and a quarter (list-price equivalent) in two minutes; most of the cost is the orchestrator reading its instructions before any work starts, and the run showed where the pipeline still relies on the model following prose.

intentCheck.basis: orchestrator check: the single paid run was made as the description says, within the allotted budget; the report carries the per-stage figures with their re-deriving commands, the added allow rules, the stall points and the quality verdict, and names no machine path

tasks.title: a with/without benchmark design fixes arms, fixture, metrics and scenarios before any run
tasks.description: docs/research/benchmark-design.md fixes the protocol before any session runs. The arms are plain Claude Code, Claude Code with the same skills and a short CLAUDE.md, and the plugin pipeline (/audit:run, /audit:resume). Each arm gets one feature-sized task in a brownfield fixture repo built fresh per run on the model of build_bench_repo.sh, and the acceptance tests are hidden from the session and applied only by the grader afterwards. Fixed across arms: model, effort, permission mode, the Claude Code CLI version (pinned, and a run on any other version refused) and the skill set (named by path and content digest, identical in the second and third arm). Every run is a fresh session, arms run in an order drawn from a recorded random seed, and cold and warm caches are reported apart. The metrics are: hidden acceptance tests passed; out-of-scope changed paths; false completion claims (claims in the final message that no tool call backs); human interventions beyond the scripted ones; wall clock; tokens by type with their list-price equivalent, naming the price source and date; and the share of the subscription window each run used, naming where that share is read and saying so when it cannot be read. The scenarios are a feature, a bugfix, an interrupted session plus resume (both sessions summed) and a step a guard must stop, with each refusal labelled by source (plugin hook, permission rule, auto-mode classifier, model refusal). Each arm runs n>=2 times in every scenario, stated as two observations rather than a variance estimate. The design also names the subscription time budget the run needs, the grading scripts it reuses, which scenarios become `claude plugin eval` cases under plugins/audit/evals/, and what the result cannot show.

outcome.technical: docs/research/benchmark-design.md: arm A plain, arm B skills plus a short CLAUDE.md, arm C is arm B plus the plugin; the fixture is built fresh per session with hidden acceptance tests and a reference solution the build refuses without; scenarios feature, bugfix, interrupted plus resume, and a guard step, with refusals labelled by source; fixed model, effort, permission mode (acceptEdits, prompts none, one allow list, a stated decision), a pinned CLI version a run refuses to differ from, and skills named by path and digest; seeded arm order, cold and warm reported apart, two observations per cell stated as such; subscription share read from the stream's rate_limit_event, dated and versioned as observed; the time budget is an open rule pending the pilot; guard and bugfix become plugin eval cases, feature and interrupted stay harness-only; prices from the official page. Every observed claim carries its date and CLI version.
outcome.descriptive: The with/without benchmark now has a fixed protocol before any session runs: three arms, one fresh brownfield fixture per session with hidden acceptance tests, four scenarios, the variables held fixed, the metrics and where each is read, and what the result cannot show.

intentCheck.basis: audit-reviewer (task mode): every element the description lists is in the document; one low finding (observed tags lacking date or version) fixed as proposed

tasks.title: the with/without benchmark runs n>=2 per arm and publishes its result with its limits
tasks.description: Runs the protocol the design fixes, at n>=2 per arm, within a subscription time budget agreed with the user before the first session. It publishes docs/research/benchmark-results.md with: the metrics the design names, per arm and scenario, each figure beside the command or grader output that re-derives it; the raw per-run records, kept in the internal repo; and a limits section (sample size, one fixture, one model, what the subscription meter could and could not show). The orchestrator runs any session that needs a human together with the user; an executor never does. If the design calls for eval cases, one case.yaml per scenario it names goes under plugins/audit/evals/. The interrupted-session scenario stays harness-only, because an eval case is one session. plugins/audit/evals/results/ is added to .gitignore, and the evals/ directory gets its line in PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md's tree. Eval paths the design does not call for are dropped from files before start. docs/README.md gains a row for the research documents.
